question: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Anchor is the status-quo random walk: 10Y CMT 5.00 on Sep 15, ~4.96-4.97 midday Sep 16 after a 4bp pullback; 12 trading sessions remain to the Oct 2 print. Over 2026 the 12-business-day change distribution is centered near zero with a modest upward drift (+126bp YTD, war/oil driven) and a 10-90 spread of roughly -0.20/+0.35, so I center at ~4.98 unconditional rather than extrapolating the last five sessions' surge. Two-sided catalysts inside the window: today's FOMC (25bp hike ~93% priced, so the risk is guidance/dots, and a credible inflation-fighting hike can cap the long end), Aug PCE ~Sep 25, quarter-end index extension Sep 30, and the Sep jobs report at 8:30 ET on resolution morning Oct 2; upside from Iran/oil escalation ($107 crude, strategist targets to 5.2%), downside from a ceasefire/oil reversal and income buyers who showed up at the 5% round number. The upper bound sits only ~29bp above spot while the lower bound is ~146bp below, so I price 11% above 5.255 (in 2026 roughly one in seven 12-day windows rose >=29bp) and no mechanism for sub-3.50; the reported percentiles are therefore right-truncated, pulling the conditional median ~2bp below spot. Evidence is one-sided toward higher yields in tone (every recent headline is a sell-off story), which is exactly when to stay near the random walk rather than chase.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) Vol: R1's 12-day SD 0.22 vs R3's 0.17/realized 0.12 is a sample-window difference (all-2026 incl. the +30bp Sep 1 jump vs Jun-Sep only); I take 0.185, which respects the September regime break without pricing the single jump as typical - so I reject R3's 0.38 width as too tight for a window containing FOMC aftermath, PCE, quarter-end and payrolls. (2) Upper-escape frequency: R1's 1-in-6/7 and R3's 5-of-61 are the same overlapping-window statistic over different samples, and both note the qualifying windows all come from the current run-up, so the higher figure double-counts one episode; reconciled to 9%, which also matches 1.6 SD on the settled vol. (3) FOMC hike odds (56% vs 93%) could not be settled from the dossiers - it looks like a timing difference in FedWatch quotes - but it is moot: the decision lands 2026-09-16T18:00Z, four days before the window opens, so it is priced by Sep 21 and only guidance transmits into the period. Settled without dispute: CR signed 2026-09-02 through Dec 11 means no funding lapse and the Oct 2 BLS print is not at risk; no usable human market exists on any venue; the CMT-vs-4pm feed ambiguity is 1-3bp and immaterial. Remaining pure-judgment tie - momentum continuation vs round-number exhaustion - is unbroken by evidence, and the bet I would take is the random walk, not the extrapolation, precisely because every recent headline runs one way.
